note.label: Psalm 79: The Heathen Have Defiled Thy Inheritance

precepts.why:
“O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.” This is not a one-time thing. It happened when Babylon besieged us first, again during the time of the Greeks who destroyed our land, and again in 70 A.D. when we were pushed out of the land. During the Greeks not all of us were pushed out and taken captive in other nations like with Babylon and 70 A.D.

Esdras tells how the temple and city were destroyed by Babylon and a remnant carried away: “As for the house of the Lord, they burnt it, and brake down the walls of Jerusalem, and set fire upon her towers: And as for her glorious things, they never ceased till they had consumed and brought them all to nought: and the people that were not slain with the sword he carried unto Babylon: Who became servants to him and his children, till the Persians reigned, to fulfil the word of the Lord spoken by the mouth of Jeremy: Until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths, the whole time of her desolation shall she rest, until the full term of seventy years.”

Even during the time of kings, our forefather King Zedekiah was taken into captivity, he and his sons and daughters. A remnant was taken captive in Babylon, which is why Daniel was born there, and they destroyed the temple and the city. That is the heathen defiling the holy temple and laying Jerusalem on heaps, with the blood of his servants shed like water and none to bury them.

note.label: Psalm 79: The Heathen Have Defiled Thy Inheritance

precepts.why:
Psalm 137 is the song of that same captivity in Babylon, the one Esdras describes, when the temple and the city were destroyed and the people not slain with the sword were carried away.

The heathen came into the inheritance and laid Jerusalem on heaps, and our people sat in Babylon as a remnant in a strange land. Our forefather King Zedekiah was taken with his sons and daughters, and Daniel was born there. That is why Psalm 79 says “We are become a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and derision to them that are round about us.” The neighbours in this context are the enemies, the other nations, the heathen, the same ones verse one says came in and defiled the temple.

precepts.text: He showed His word unto Jacob and His judgments unto Israel; He has not dealt so with any nation.
precepts.point: The heathen having "not known thee" does not mean there are heathen who do know the Lord. To know God is to keep His commandments, and the commandments were only given to the israelites. The other nations do not truly know God, His ways, or His judgments; we do.

note.label: Psalm 79: The Heathen Have Defiled Thy Inheritance

precepts.why:
The prayer asks the Most High to “Pour out thy wrath upon the heathen that have not known thee, and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon thy name.” The heathen having not known thee does not mean there are heathen who do know the Lord.

Psalm 147 settles it: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.” He showed his word unto Jacob and his judgments unto Israel; he has not dealt so with any nation.

To know God is to keep his commandments, and the commandments were only given to the israelites. The other nations do not truly know God, his ways or his judgments; we do. So the wrath poured out on the heathen that have not known him is wrath on those who “devoured Jacob, and laid waste his dwelling place”, the nations who were never given his judgments.

precepts.text: The heathen came into the Most High's inheritance, defiled His holy temple, and laid Jerusalem on heaps.
precepts.point: All her people sigh and seek bread, and they gave their pleasant things for meat to relieve the soul; when things get that serious, people give up whatever they once thought they could not live without.

note.label: Lamentations 1: The City That Sits Solitary

precepts.why:
Jerusalem “hath seen that the heathen entered into her sanctuary, whom thou didst command that they should not enter into thy congregation.” The psalm mourns the same thing: “O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.”

The heathen came into the Most High's inheritance, defiled His holy temple, and laid Jerusalem on heaps. That is why she is removed, why “all that honoured her despise her”, and why she has no comforter: she grievously sinned, and the ones the Most High commanded should not enter His congregation walked into her sanctuary.

moments.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled. The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the heaven; their blood have they shed like water round about Jerusalem. We are become a reproach to our neighbours. Pour out thy wrath upon the heathen that have not known thee.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Wherefore should the heathen say, Where is their God? That is blasphemy. Through the whole captivity, through the ships, the auction blocks, the plantations, the terror, and even now through the ghettos and the poisons put in our communities, the taunt has been the same: where is your God? Every taunt of it is blasphemy against the Most High, and he has heard every word.
